title: Cloud sessions checked end to end with real OpenSSH and a real model
request: The owner's goal: the same capabilities as Claude Code and Codex, proven; the owner's server was not yet available.
plan: a throwaway sshd as the owner's user on loopback, key-only
a second DCLab Code as the server
connect, a real model session there, copy records, the store keeps them, disconnect, stop everything

decisions.decision: a user-level sshd on 127.0.0.1 instead of macOS Remote Login
decisions.why: no system setting is changed and nothing is reachable from outside; it is stopped afterwards

decisions.decision: wrap ssh only to add -F with the scratch config
decisions.why: DCLab Code's own ssh arguments stay exactly what a real server gets

change: no product code; the live-test driver, the server's home and the README in R&D agent_runs/live_tests/2026-10-26-dclab-code-remote/, docs.

measurements.name: live
measurements.gate: real ssh opens the tunnel, a real model session runs on the other DCLab Code, its record is copied and kept by the store, the tunnel closes
measurements.result: tunnel in 1.9 s on port 47154; Haiku answered from README.md, $0.005; 1 record, 12 KB, copied; the keeper lists it; no ssh left

outcome: Cloud sessions work end to end with the real tools; only a real network and the owner's server remain.
lessons: When the real target is not available, make every part real but the distance, and say what is left uncovered.
risks: not across a real network or on the owner's server
